result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give clear role tables, careful date formatting and solid system-font stacks. B makes shelf codes harder to misread: it uses a monospace with distinct 0/O and 1/l/I, tabular alignment and no wrapping. It also adds Intl date formatting, rem scaling, contrast guidance and a check for thermal printing. A's one-family plan is well argued and its specimen test is a very concrete check, but it only falls back to a font with distinct characters if that test fails, and it covers less detail overall. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers are strong and cover nearly the same ground. A's monospace for shelf codes is well argued, and its advice to get the installed font list is concrete. B edges ahead because it labels its sizes as starting points to test, gives an explicit test string (Oo0 Il1, QB 412.7) to render on the kiosk, and breaks the plan down screen by screen. Its single-family choice is also justified, with monospace kept as a backup if the test fails.
